faq: What does this tool calculate?
Speed from pace: 60 ÷ the minutes per unit distance, in km/h and mph, from a min/km or min/mile input.
Is the result exact?
The inversion is exact arithmetic on the pace you enter; rounding in the display is to a decimal, shown openly.
Do I need an account?
No. A pace in, a speed out.
Does the route include live traffic?
No — your legs set the speed; traffic is for the wheels in the other tools.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Your pace was measured over the path you ran, which is the distance the speed honestly describes.
Which pace unit should I enter?
The one your plan or watch uses. The outputs cover both speed systems either way.
The reverse — speed to pace?
The Speed to Pace Calculator inverts this one, as its name promises.
What speed is a 20-minute 5K pace?
4:00/km → 15.0 km/h. The calculator turns goal paces into speeds your watch can shout about.
Walking pace 12:00/km?
5.0 km/h — a purposeful walk, and now a speed a guidebook would nod at.
Why do treadmills top out at odd paces?
Because their speeds are round (10, 12, 16 km/h) and paces are the reciprocals — the oddness lives in the inversion, not the machine.
